event.name: 25 October 2018 Mw 6.8 Zakynthos earthquake (Ionian Sea, Greece)
event.tectonic_setting: Intraslab rupture of subducted Ionian oceanic crust at the Cephalonia Transform Fault–western Hellenic subduction junction. Distinct from interplate megathrust slip.
event.region: Offshore southwest Zakynthos, Ionian Sea, Greece

reference.title: Intraslab Deformation and Rupture of the Entire Subducting Crust During the 25 October 2018 Mw 6.8 Zakynthos Earthquake

inversion.method: Joint wavelet-domain kinematic finite-fault inversion (Ji et al. 2002) using teleseismic waveforms, near-fault strong-motion records, static GPS offsets and high-rate GPS. Simulated annealing with Laplacian smoothing constraints on slip and rupture time; model plotted in Figure 2a.
inversion.green_function_model: Frequency–wavenumber Green functions (Zhu and Rivera, 2001) using a 1-D velocity model for the Zakynthos region (Papadimitriou et al., 2012).
inversion.notes: FIGURE-DIGITIZED scalar slip from Chousianitis & Konca (2019) Figure 2a (PDF page 5), NOT author-released inversion values. The ORIGINAL grid is 33 along-strike x 27 down-dip patches of 2 x 2 km on a 66 x 54 km plane, strike 14 deg, dip 49 deg east, top depth 3 km (Section 2). Image chart uses signed along-strike coordinate about -22 to +44 km; output along_strike_km is shifted to [0,66] measured from left chart edge, not geographic northing. Absolute depth_km uses top depth + down_dip_km * sin(49deg). The non-horizontal plot y axis is DEPTH, not down-dip length; the image samples were taken on the existing 27 rendered patch rows, not interpreted as vertical 2-km cells. Slip samples are CIELAB-nearest palette matches to the printed 0-1.5m colorbar with saturated pixel filtering to reject black RUPTURE-TIME contours (2.5s spacing), white variable-rake slip arrows and the red hypocenter star. Per-patch values are rounded to 0.01 m for display, but digitization uncertainty may exceed 0.1-0.2 m under obscuring overlays. Nominal rake 167 deg is a schema-compatible surrogate from a different published nodal-plane mechanism for the same earthquake (Cirella et al. 2020 preferred NP1); it is NOT a reported Chousianitis-Konca inverted mean rake or local rake. Figure 2a shows variable slip-vector directions that are NOT digitized. This nominal rake must not be used to compute physically rigorous vector slip or moment. The publication reports 1.4m peak at ~17km depth; 0.52m mean for patches exceeding 10% of published peak; approximately one third of cells above threshold. The 0.17m mean stored in summary_metrics is IMAGE-DERIVED over ALL 891 cells, not a published author summary. Image-derived low slip/colorbar bottom values do not prove exact zero. The paper supplies the revised NOA hypocenter (37.341N,20.512E,10km) whereas the existing Cirella model cites a different relocated location; these are retained independently for event grouping. Origin_time was normalized to the existing Cirella et al. geobrowser event record at 22:54:50.09Z for consistent automatic grouping; this paper specifies only 22:54 GMT in its text. Individual patch latitude/longitude omitted because a georeferenced top-left plane corner is not provided by Figure 2a.

provenance.compiled_by: Colorbar-calibrated digitization of original full-resolution Figure 2a (page 5) from user-provided Chousianitis & Konca 2019 PDF; 891 published 2-km squares preserved, no resampling. Original scalar slip coefficients not available.
